rationale.org-governance: Derives three orientations and twelve project-level governance strategies from OSS policies.
rationale.oversight-scaling-inversion: Empirically documents cheap generation overwhelming scarce maintainer review capacity.
rationale.quality-debt: Policies focalize correctness, complexity, maintainability, and low-value AI contributions.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Documents test-log and proof-of-concept requirements as submission gates.
rationale.risk-routing: Independent queue limits route excess newcomer PRs away from reviewer attention.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Prior-issue approvals and mandatory human review create authoritative lifecycle checkpoints.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Disclosure, validation notes, and evidence make AI contributions judgeable.
rationale.agent-scope-drift: Issue-linking and focused-PR rules bound AI changes to approved intent.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Persistent PR disclosures record AI use and provenance for review.
rationale.survey-input: Orientation prevalence and strategy patterns can inform governance survey design.
rationale.counterpoint: Opposes reducing GenAI governance to a binary ban-or-allow question.
rationale.assistive: Corpus includes policies governing human-led AI-assisted contribution workflows.
rationale.agentic: Corpus includes autonomous agents delivering repository-scale patches and PRs.
rationale.steering: Tool-facing instructions substantively constrain agents before contribution generation.
rationale.risk-security: Analyzes evidence gates protecting vulnerability channels from fabricated AI reports.
rationale.risk-quality: Reports focal concerns about correctness, maintainability, complexity, and reviewability.
rationale.risk-ip: Focally analyzes copyright, licensing, provenance uncertainty, and safeguards.
rationale.method-mining: Qualitatively codes repository policies, templates, threads, and governance artifacts.
